channel.title: THE HUMANS ARE FINE.
channel.description: Independent AI journalism. Every story carries a public Evidence File.

item.title: OpenAI Is Treating Its New Cheap Model as "Critical" for Cybersecurity. It Went on Sale the Same Day.
item.description: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra at half the price of the model it replaces, stating the Critical cybersecurity determination in a single sentence. Its own system card says OpenAI is treating the model as Critical for cybersecurity and rates it High for biological and chemical capability. The announcement mentions the first and not the second.

item.title: England's Most Senior Civil Judge Says Chatbots Are Driving a Surge in Court Claims. The Government's Own Statistics Point at Parking Tickets.
item.description: Days from retirement, Geoffrey Vos says a 10 percent annual rise in county court claims is down to people consulting Gemini, ChatGPT and Claude. The Ministry of Justice's own quarterly bulletin, published in September, points at claims over parking on private land — and shows the category he wants automated getting smaller.

item.title: Google Says Its New World Model Generates Its Own Sound, and Characters That Talk Back
item.description: DeepMind's Genie 4 builds interactive worlds from a sentence, gives them voices, and admits the worlds drift. It publishes no result from the safety tests it says it ran.

item.title: Anthropic Tests Reveal Weaknesses in AI Coding-Agent Security Monitors
item.description: Anthropic's red-team research found substantial bypass success against the blocking monitors used in Claude Code's Auto Mode and in OpenAI's Codex, the Guardian variant tested being an approximation of Codex's production default. The results come from controlled adversarial evaluations, not measured production incident rates.

item.title: Anthropic Researchers Try Deleting a Model's Cheating Instead of Punishing It
item.description: A training method routes a model's cheating into parameters that are then deleted. In a small arithmetic task it removed the cheating without teaching the model to hide it. The authors call the work preliminary.

item.title: An Outside Red Team Found Ways Around OpenAI's Own Agent Monitors
item.description: METR and Redwood Research stress-tested OpenAI's internal misalignment monitoring. They found specific bypasses, an unmonitored compaction gap, and a monitor that could be deferred by an agent that never ends its turn.

item.title: Learned to Invent Problems, Until Its Makers Changed the Reward
item.description: Training an auditor on the wrong reward produced one that invented findings. Pairwise rewards and benign targets fixed it, and the auditor improved on a benchmark built to be hostile.
